title: Perf/telemetry: reduce cardinality in dedicated rollout + gate metrics (aggregation labels + sampling)
author: Thomas Baird
description:
Context: during dogfood of Dedicated staged rollouts we saw sustained TSDB churn + slow queries caused by high-cardinality labels on rollout/gate metrics (pool_id x rollout_plan_id x stage_id x gate_id x plan_version x region, etc). This PR reduces cardinality by (1) introducing a stable set of aggregation labels (tenant, pool, rollout_kind, stage_index, gate_type, result) and removing per-object identifiers from metric labels, and (2) adding deterministic sampling for high-volume pools so we keep signal without exploding series count. This is specifically for rollout/gate evaluation metrics and the Console status aggregation endpoints that query them.

Changes: - Replace label sets on rollout gate evaluation metrics: drop rollout_plan_id, rollout_plan_version, stage_id, gate_id; add rollout_kind={dedicated_staged}, stage_index (int), gate_type (latency_p95|error_rate_5xx|timeout_rate|queue_depth|gpu_util), and evaluation_window_sec bucket. - Add `rollouts.metrics.sample_rate` (default 1.0) and deterministic sampler keyed by (tenant_id, pool_id) to include/exclude emission for high-volume pools. Sampling is applied to per-evaluation outcome metrics; counters for evaluator health are NOT sampled. - Emit two tiers of metrics: (a) low-cardinality always-on "health" metrics for evaluator loop + metric freshness, and (b) sampled per-gate outcome metrics for dashboards/alerts. - Add guardrails in metric emitter to cap free-form label values and normalize gate_type to a small enum. - Backwards-compat: old metrics are still emitted behind `rollouts.metrics.emit_legacy=true` (default false in staging, true in prod for 1 week). Added log warning on startup when legacy emission is enabled.

Why deterministic sampling: we want stable series (so dashboards/alerts don’t flap) and to avoid biasing toward bursty pools. Hash-based sampling by pool keeps inclusion stable over time.

Testing: - Unit tests for label normalization + sampler determinism. - Added a synthetic high-cardinality regression test in `telemetry/tests` that fails if series key count exceeds threshold for a representative rollout plan. - Verified dashboards queries against new labels in staging (see notes below).

Operational notes: - This PR does not change gating behavior, only what we emit and how we aggregate. - If you need per-gate debugging, use structured logs (gate evaluator emits gate_id/stage_id in logs) and the rollout audit event stream. - Follow-up: update dashboards in observability-pack (tracked in ENG-5131 / separate PR).

Staging verification (02/20): - Evaluator outcome series count reduced ~18x on `dedicated-dogfood-west` after removing gate_id/stage_id labels. - p95 query time for rollout dashboards dropped from ~9-12s to ~1.5-2s (PromQL).
commits: telemetry: add rollout_metrics_label_set_v2 and gate_type enum normalization
gate-evaluator: wire v2 metric emitter + deterministic pool sampler
telemetry: add regression test for series key explosion
config: add rollouts.metrics.sample_rate and legacy emission toggle
docs/comments: annotate dashboards queries to use stage_index/gate_type
review_conversation:
Logan Wright (review): Can we guarantee gate_type stays low-cardinality? I’m worried someone adds a new gate and accidentally uses a stringified name again. Also: sampling should not apply to evaluator health metrics; those are the first thing we look at during incidents.

Thomas Baird (author): Yep. I added `GateType` as an enum w/ a closed set + `unknown` and a unit test that fails if a gate tries to emit an arbitrary string label. Sampling only wraps `rollout_gate_eval_total` + `rollout_gate_eval_duration_ms`; evaluator loop health metrics remain always-on.

Allison Grant (review): For dashboards, stage_index is OK but we still need to break down by pool_id and tenant_id. Confirm those labels remain. Also please add a brief comment in the query helper so future edits don’t reintroduce gate_id.

Thomas Baird (author): Confirmed: tenant_id and pool_id remain. Added comments in `console-backend/rollouts/status/metrics_query.go` and an assertion in the query builder that rejects disallowed labels.

Sean Gallagher (review): What happens when sample_rate < 1 and a pool is excluded—do our alerts miss real gate failures? We should still alert on “rollout paused” based on state machine, but some early warning graphs might go quiet.

Thomas Baird (author): Agree. The paging alerts are based on rollout state/audit events and evaluator health (unsampled). The sampled metrics are for trend graphs + non-paging warnings. I updated the runbook note in PR description and ensured `rollout_paused_total` remains unsampled.

Chloe Martin (review): Console query helper now groups by stage_index/gate_type; do we need evaluation_window_sec to avoid mixing windows? I saw windows vary by gate.

Thomas Baird (author): Good catch—added `evaluation_window_sec` as a label (bucketed to a small set). Console status endpoint uses the window configured for the stage; the label prevents mixing in ad hoc queries.

CI note: first run failed telemetry-regression-suite due to old expected label set. Updated fixtures and reran; now green.

Approval: Logan + Allison approved after changes. Sean approved with note to coordinate dashboard changes with ENG-5131.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main on 2025-02-21 by Connor O'Brien. Squash commit: 8f2c1e6a9c2e. Release: included in next Dedicated rollouts dogfood train (feature flags unchanged).
release_notes: Internal: Reduced cardinality of rollout/gate evaluation metrics and added deterministic sampling for high-volume Dedicated pools to improve dashboard query performance and TSDB stability. No change to gating decisions or rollout state machine.
